instruction: Switch the system clock to 12-hour format.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to display battery percentage on a VM without a battery. Opened system menu, navigated to Settings > Power > Appearance, then opened Terminal and ran 'gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface show-battery-percentage true'. The setting was applied but the task was infeasible (no battery in VM).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system menu, navigate GNOME Settings sections, search and open Terminal via Activities, execute gsettings commands to change system configuration
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to recognize the task as infeasible. The VM has no battery, so displaying battery percentage is impossible. Model should have output [INFEASIBLE] but instead tried to enable the setting.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a concrete gsettings change task (clock format) within model's demonstrated capability of navigating settings and using gsettings commands
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the GNOME clock format to 12-hour. Evaluator checks gsettings output contains '12h'. Model can achieve this through Settings UI or gsettings command.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-format' to read the GNOME clock format setting, which is the exact command needed to verify 12-hour format.

Metric check_include_exclude correctly receives the rules dict (include=['12h'], exclude=[]) and checks if '12h' is contained in the gsettings output. The output will be '12h' when set to 12-hour format, so the substring check works correctly.
Full instruction coverage: the single requirement (switch to 12-hour format) is fully verified by checking the clock-format gsettings key.
No postconfig needed since gsettings is a command-line query that reads system state directly without UI dependency.
Parameter handling is correct: with expected.type='rule', the framework passes the rules dict directly to check_include_exclude, which expects (result, rules) with 'include' and 'exclude' keys.
